title: Confidence Exploitation: Do Student Models Learn to Appear More Confident to Satisfy Overseers?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Unjustified confidence is a concrete safety risk. If oversight training creates confident-but-wrong models, this identifies a training-induced safety hazard. Clear and actionable finding.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Measuring expressed confidence requires defining a confidence metric (e.g., hedging language frequency, probability calibration). Training under oversight requires existing setup. Moderate complexity for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Requires tracking confidence over training, correlating with overseer rating and actual accuracy. Three variables to measure and correlate. Focused but requires some statistical analysis. Feasible in 30 hours with guidance.
